name: Lion El’Jonson
early: Survived alone among Caliban’s predatory, Chaos-tainted beasts before adoption. The duration and details are inconsistent across accounts; this is an early-life survival precedent, not a measured first-hour feat.
adult: Supreme hunter and duellist; defeated daemon Angron after his return. Forestwalking is a later revealed ability, not a general infant Primarch trait.
comparison: Primus has no demonstrated equivalence in swordsmanship, hunting experience, or forestwalking.

name: Fulgrim
early: Adopted on Chemos. Angel Exterminatus presents a distinctly supernatural arrival, including contact with a finder’s mind. His industrial reforms belong to later development, not the moment the pod opens.
adult: Exceptional duellist, craftsman and industrial reformer; killed Ferrus in circumstances involving the Laer blade. Later daemonhood changes the comparison.
comparison: Primus is not demonstrated to match Fulgrim’s complete martial or creative repertoire. No automatic copying of Fulgrim’s emergence glamour.

name: Perturabo
early: Wandered Olympia before adoption, associated with beast-slaying. His earliest remembered scene is climbing a mountain; he exhibits extraordinary pre-existing intellectual ability. The whole wandering period cannot be labelled his first day.
adult: Master of engineering, siegecraft and battlefield calculation; brought daemon Angron under control with preparation, firepower and disciplined tactics.
comparison: Primus is an exceptional operative, not a demonstrated peer of Perturabo in engineering or theatre command.

name: Jaghatai Khan
early: Found by Ong Khan’s people and raised among the Talskars. Became an exceptional young warrior; vengeance for his foster father and campaigns of unification occur later.
adult: Extraordinary speed, swordsmanship and mobile warfare; banished daemon Mortarion at the cost of catastrophic injury.
comparison: No evidence places Primus at the Khan’s peak duelling speed or campaign mastery.

name: Leman Russ
early: Raised by Fenrisian wolves. Fought human hunters but was captured, then learned human speech and weapons. Mammoth-wrestling and army-breaking stories are later feats, not verified pod-emergence events.
adult: Primarch duellist and hunter; defeated Magnus on Prospero and wounded empowered Horus using the Emperor’s spear. Equipment and circumstances matter.
comparison: Primus’s active psychic range does not establish physical or duelling parity with Russ.

name: Rogal Dorn
early: Raised by the House of Dorn on Inwit. Detailed pod-emergence feats are poorly documented; later rulership and restoration of Phalanx cannot supply an infant strength measurement.
adult: Master of fortification and strategic defence; personally killed Alpharius on Pluto.
comparison: Primus has no demonstrated equivalent to Dorn’s full battlefield presence, combat record or strategic command.

name: Konrad Curze
early: The traditional account has his capsule penetrate deep into Nostramo and the child escape to the surface. He then survived without a foster family. Exact depth, travel time and infant physiology are not reliable engineering measurements.
adult: Lethal ambusher and duellist with precognition; repeatedly endangered other Primarchs through surprise and foresight.
comparison: Primus has no established equivalent to Curze’s particular foresight or predatory stealth.

name: Sanguinius
early: Killed a Baalite fire scorpion before his adoption. An account describes walking within weeks and exceeding human stature within a year. This supports lethal early capability but not a universal maturation schedule.
adult: Flight, precognition and exceptional melee power; defeated Ka’Bandha and daemon Angron during the Siege of Terra.
comparison: Primus has not demonstrated this combination or equivalent apex victories.

name: Ferrus Manus
early: Survived Medusa’s mountains and hostile technological remnants. The defeat of Asirnoth in magma belongs to his later wandering; it is not securely dated to immediately leaving the pod. Accounts differ on his apparent development.
adult: Exceptional strength, craftsmanship and warfare; his legendary contest with the Emperor devastated the landscape. Killed by Fulgrim at Isstvan V.
comparison: Primus’s strength is above ordinary Astartes, but no evidence supports Ferrus-level brute force or metallurgy.

name: Angron
early: Defeated numerous armed xenos shortly after arrival and was found grievously wounded among their corpses. The older account describes scores of corpses; his subsequent capture must be read in the context of severe prior injury, not as a demonstration that healthy child Angron was physically comparable to human captors. The exact number and alleged Farseer, Aspect Warrior or Ranger composition are not verified here.
adult: Extraordinary close-combat strength; supported a descending Warhound foot briefly while severely strained. Daemon ascension later greatly changes his powers and resilience.
comparison: Primus has no demonstrated equivalent to Angron’s peak physical feats; his psychic options make this more than a strength contest.

name: Roboute Guilliman
early: Found and adopted by Konor on Macragge. A rapidly developing prodigy; extensive learning and the Illyrian campaign belong to his upbringing, not a recorded pod-opening battle.
adult: Primarch combatant and exceptional organiser of armies and civilisations. Divine intervention during Godblight is not a repeatable measure of his unassisted power.
comparison: Primus is not shown to match Guilliman’s overall physical and strategic capability, although he has far more overt psychic practice.

name: Mortarion
early: Survived Barbarus’s toxic atmosphere and was taken by Necare, who tested his tolerance while raising him. His eventual rebellion and assault on Necare’s highest refuge occur later.
adult: Exceptional endurance and attritional warfare; daemonhood adds Nurgle’s supernatural gifts and sorcery.
comparison: Primus has no established equivalence in toxin resistance, endurance or daemon manifestations.

name: Magnus the Red
early: Aware during gestation and remembers infancy; communed psychically with the Emperor before their physical reunion. Learned under Amon and surpassed his teachers. Not a blank-minded child in every respect.
adult: The psychic outlier among Primarchs, with immense projection and sorcery. The Webway breach involved external help; later daemon feats cannot be treated as unaided mortal output.
comparison: Primus is an exceptional Astartes psyker, but there is no sound basis for calling him sixty percent of Magnus’s greatest workings.

name: Horus Lupercal
early: Lupus Daemonis portrays him as Nergüi, a young Cthonian ganger whose buried knowledge and physical development awaken dramatically later. This complicates any single smooth growth curve for all Primarchs.
adult: Exceptional commander and combatant. His final confrontation with the Emperor follows vast Chaos empowerment and is outside the ordinary Primarch baseline.
comparison: Primus cannot meaningfully be scored as a fraction of final-battle Horus; unascended Horus remains the useful comparison.

name: Lorgar Aurelian
early: Taken in by desert nomads; seventeen days later reportedly the size of a small child. Learned under Kor Phaeron and later killed mutineers to protect him. Physical power did not prevent manipulation or dependency.
adult: Developed formidable sorcery and ritual leadership; grew substantially beyond his early-Heresy reputation. Daemonhood changes the scale again.
comparison: Primus’s practical psychic feats do not establish superiority to mature Lorgar’s sorcery or a fixed duel outcome.

name: Vulkan
early: Adopted by the smith N’bel. Surpassed local adults in size, strength and smithcraft within three years; the famous defence against Dark Eldar occurs in his fourth year, not at pod emergence.
adult: Exceptional strength and craftsmanship, with Perpetual regeneration. Regeneration is a distinct capability, not simply a high durability score.
comparison: Primus has no demonstrated Perpetual resurrection or equivalent smithing record. Neither is inherited by our subject.

name: Corvus Corax
early: Found by Lycaean prisoners, hidden and educated for leadership and rebellion. Possessed extraordinary natural gifts, but the liberation campaign followed preparation and teaching.
adult: Supernatural concealment, infiltration and Primarch combat ability. His later Warp manifestation against Lorgar is a different state from childhood.
comparison: Primus has no demonstrated equivalent to Corax’s specific concealment or later Warp transformation.

name: Alpharius / Omegon
early: Origin accounts deliberately conflict. Head of the Hydra claims a Terran arrival for one twin and an isolated alien world for the other. This is weak evidence for a universal emergence benchmark.
adult: Primarch combatants specialised in deception, covert warfare and concealment of presence; their twin nature is a distinct trait.
comparison: There is no reliable head-to-head rating with Primus. Do not transfer twin-soul or identity powers to the subject.

name: The II and XI Primarchs
early: No reliable published emergence record sufficient for this comparison. Leave unknown.
adult: Insufficient evidence for a peak-power comparison.
comparison: No responsible numerical rating is possible.
